'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[July 2021 Gulf of Oman incident]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] and the [[United States]] join [[Israel]] in blaming [[Iran]] for the strike. [[British Foreign Secretary]] [[Dominic Raab]] says that the UK and its allies are planning a coordinated response. However, an [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian Foreign Ministry]] spokesperson says the allegation is "baseless." [https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-business-iran-persian-gulf-tensions-419efc522acbd213a79696c9876af6dc?repost (AP)] [https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/565845-us-blames-iran-for-attack-on-oil-tanker-off-oman-forwarding-statement (''The Hill'')]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[2021 Niger attacks]]
***Fifteen [[Niger Armed Forces|troops]] are killed and six others are missing as [[Islamism|Islamists]] [[ambush]] them in [[Torodi]], [[Tillabéri Region]], [[Niger]]. A bomb also explodes as the soldiers tried to evacuate their wounded. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20210801-more-than-a-dozens-soldiers-killed-several-missing-in-niger-attack (France 24)]
*[[Central African Republic Civil War]]
**Militants belonging to the [[Return, Reclamation, Rehabilitation|3R]] group attack a [[Central African Armed Forces|military]] position in the village of Mann, [[Central African Republic]], killing six civilians and wounding several more. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/six-civilians-killed-several-wounded-in-car-rebel-attack (Al Jazeera)]
*Five people, including three [[Hezbollah]] members, are killed and several more are wounded as gunmen open fire at the funeral of Ali Shibli, a Hezbollah member who was assassinated yesterday in [[Khalde]], [[Lebanon]]. Both the attacks are described as motivated by [[Anti-Shi'ism|anti-shi'ism]] and as a revenge for the killing of a [[Sunni Islam|Sunni]] [[Arab]] teenager and a [[Syrians in Lebanon|Syrian]] last year in the same town. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210801-three-hezbollah-among-5-dead-in-lebanon-funeral-ambush-security-source (France 24)]

'''Arts and culture'''
**[[YouTube]] bans [[News Corp]]'s ''[[Sky News Australia]]'' channel from uploading new content for seven days after commentator [[Alan Jones (radio broadcaster)|Alan Jones]] spreads [[COVID-19 misinformation]]. This comes shortly after ''[[The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)|The Daily Telegraph]]'' fired Jones and ended his regular column over similar concerns. According to a YouTube spokesman, "Specifically, we don’t allow content that denies the existence of Covid-19 or that encourages people to use hydroxychloroquine or ivermectin to treat or prevent the virus." [https://www.theguardian.com/media/2021/aug/01/sky-news-australia-banned-from-youtube-for-seven-days-over-covid-misinformation (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Canada]] observes "[[Emancipation Day]]" nationwide for the first time. The holiday, commemorating the day in 1834 when the [[Slavery Abolition Act 1833]] came into force and outlawed [[slavery in Canada]] and most of the [[British Empire]], was unanimously declared by [[Parliament of Canada|Parliament]] in March. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/canada-marks-first-ever-nationwide-emancipation-day (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Prime Minister of New Zealand|New Zealand Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] formally apologizes to the [[Pacific Islander]] community for the [[Dawn Raids (New Zealand)|Dawn Raids]], a series of [[New Zealand Police|police]] [[police raid|raids]] in the 1970s that targeted and deported Pacific Islanders accused of overstaying their [[work visa]]s, and says that the [[government of New Zealand|government]] will create new education and training [[scholarship]]s for the community, and an official account of the raids in order to compensate for them. The apology was supposed to happen in June, but it was delayed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand|COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/new-zealand-apologizes-for-1970s-dawn-raids (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Afghanistan flood]]
**[[Flash flood]]ing continues for the fourth day in [[Kamdesh District]], [[Nuristan Province]], killing several more people and bringing the death toll to 113. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/death-toll-afghanistan-floods-tops-100-dozens-still-missing (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Turkish wildfires]]
**The death toll from [[wildfire]]s in southern [[Turkey]] rises to eight. Thousands of [[Tourism in Turkey|tourists]] are evacuated from [[Bodrum]] by the [[Coast Guard Command (Turkey)|Coast Guard Command]] as the fires close in on the port city. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/some-wildfires-rage-turkey-although-most-have-been-contained-2021-08-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] begins a [[COVID-19]] vaccination rollout for teenagers between the ages of 12 and 17 years using the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] vaccine. [[Prime Minister of Cambodia|Prime Minister]] [[Hun Sen]]'s grandchildren are among the first to receive the vaccine. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210801-cambodia-begins-covid-19-vaccinations-for-teenagers (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]] lifts its travel restrictions for the first time since March 2020 for tourists who have been [[COVID-19 vaccination in Saudi Arabia|vaccinated]] against COVID-19 using government-approved [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]s. Vaccinated travelers must register themselves on the data registration portal introduced by the [[Ministry of Tourism of Saudi Arabia|Ministry of Tourism]], which also requires a negative PCR test from the previous 72 hours. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/saudi-arabia-to-reopen-for-tourists-vaccinated-with-approved-jabs-from-today-101627779119174.html (''Hindustan Times'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] extends its semi-[[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] measures in 13 [[Provinces of Thailand|province]]s including the [[Bangkok Metropolitan Region]] until August 31 and also extends the restrictions into 16 additional provinces beginning on August 3 due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases in the country. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-08-01/thailand-expands-strict-covid-curbs-to-cover-40-of-population (Bloomberg News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Nigeria]]
****[[Nigeria]] receives four million doses of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] from [[Government of the United States|U.S. government]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2021/08/01/nigeria-receives-four-million-covid-vacine-doses-from-the-us/ (Africanews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Tunisia]]
****[[Tunisia]] receives 1.5 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccine from [[Italy]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/coronavirus/2021/08/01/Crisis-hit-Tunisia-receives-1-5-mln-COVID-19-vaccines-from-Italy (Al Arabiya)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****The number of patients hospitalized due to COVID-19 in [[Florida]] reaches a record 10,207, surpassing the previous record of 10,170 people recorded on July 23, 2020. [https://apnews.com/article/business-health-florida-coronavirus-pandemic-7ca97f0d685ab25559cf9b51cfc077eb (Associated Press)]
***The U.S. surpasses 35 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/u-s-passes-35-million-covid-cases-california-tops-4-n1275658 (NBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***[[Germany]] begins to require any travelers over the age of 12 years old who have been not fully [[COVID-19 vaccination|vaccinated]] or recovered from COVID-19, regardless of transportation mode, to present a negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test result]] taken within the previous 48 hours for [[rapid antigen test]]s and 72 hours for [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] tests amidst concerns of the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/germanys-stricter-rules-for-unvaccinated-travelers-take-effect/a-58718980 (Deutsche Welle)]

'''International relations'''
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[Kim Jong-un]]'s sister [[Kim Yo-jong]] warns [[South Korea]] against conducting military drills with the [[United States]], saying that such a move could damage the talks to resolve the [[Korean conflict]]. The two [[Korea]]s have been improving relations lately, with North Korea restoring the [[North Korea-South Korea border|border]] hotlines, which Kim Yo-jong called a "physical" measure in case the drills take place. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/nkorean-leaders-sister-warns-seoul-against-military-drill-with-washington-2021-08-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Five high-ranking [[Madagascar People's Armed Forces|army officers]] and several police officers are arrested in [[Madagascar]] in connection with a failed attempt to [[assassinate]] [[Andry Rajoelina|the country's president]], thereby bringing the number of people arrested in connection to the plot to 21. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58050276 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**On the six-month anniversary of the [[coup]], [[Tatmadaw|military]] [[Junta (governing body)|junta]] leader [[Min Aung Hlaing]] names himself [[Prime Minister of Myanmar|Prime Minister]] "in order to perform [[Myanmar|the country]]’s duties fast, easily and effectively", according to the ruling [[State Administration Council]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/myanmar-military-leader-takes-new-title-prime-minister-caretaker-government-2021-08-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Formula One World Championship]]
**[[2021 Hungarian Grand Prix]]
***[[Formula One drivers from France|French racing driver]] [[Esteban Ocon]] of [[Alpine F1 Team|Alpine]] wins the first [[Formula One]] race of his career. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/08/01/motorsport/hungarian-grand-prix-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2020 Summer Olympics]]
**[[Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
***[[United States at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
****[[United States|American]] [[Shot put|shot putter]] [[Raven Saunders]] raises and crosses her arms in the [[X mark|shape of an X]] while participating in the [[Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's shot put|Women's shot put]] medal ceremony. Podium demonstrations are banned by the [[International Olympic Committee]], with the IOC announcing an investigation to the incident. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/08/02/sport/raven-saunders-podium-protest-olympics-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
***[[Belarus at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
****[[Belarus|Belarusian]] [[Sprint (running)|sprinter]] [[Krystsina Tsimanouskaya]] is [[Belarus 2020 Summer Olympics scandal|forcibly removed]] from the Games by the [[Belarus Olympic Committee]] after criticizing officials for entering her in the [[Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's 4 × 400 metres relay|4 by 400 meter relay race]] without her consent. Tsimanouskaya has appealed to the [[IOC]] for support and asked [[Tokyo police|Japanese police]] for protection at [[Haneda Airport]] after she refused to board a flight to [[Belarus]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/tokyo-olympics-belarusian-athlete-tsimanouskaya-forced-to-leave-games/a-58722997 (Deutsche Welle)]
***[[Italy at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
****[[Italy|Italian]] [[sprint (running)|sprinter]] [[Marcell Jacobs]] wins the [[Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres|men's 100-metres final]] in an Olympics upset, [[100_metres#All-time_top_25_men|tying as the 10th-fastest man of all time]]. [https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/athletics-italian-jacobs-wins-mens-100m-gold-tokyo-olympics-2021-08-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 CONCACAF Gold Cup]]
**In [[association football]], the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] defeats [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] 1–0 after [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] in the [[2021 CONCACAF Gold Cup Final|final]] to win their seventh Gold Cup title. [https://www.straitstimes.com/sport/football/football-usa-stun-mexico-in-extra-time-to-win-gold-cup (''The Straits Times'')]
